title: Police question Abhishek Banerjee for nearly four hours over 'Gujarati gang' post
dek: The Trinamool Congress general secretary answered Kolkata Police questions over a May post about the Chief Election Commissioner, and has been summoned again on 20 November in a separate case.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Trinamool Congress national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee was questioned for nearly four hours at Bhowanipore police station in Kolkata on Saturday over a social media post that allegedly described Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar as a puppet of an "anti-Bengali Gujarati gang".

The Diamond Harbour MP arrived at about 12.20 pm, shortly before the 12.30 pm time in the police notice, and left in the late afternoon; reports differ on the time, with one putting it at about 4 pm and another at 4.34 pm. Speaking to reporters afterwards, he accused the state's BJP government of harassment. "This will continue; it has been continuing for 6 months," he said. "Police notice will come, bulldozer will come, put pressure, put me in jail, I will still not bow down."

## The case

The FIR was registered on 27 May on a complaint by a Bhowanipore resident, who alleged that Mr Banerjee's post of 2 May used negative language about Gujarati people. The post responded to BJP leader Amit Malviya's post about Falta in Mr Banerjee's constituency, and challenged the Union government to "Come to Falta". It was registered under several sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including promoting enmity between groups and making statements conducive to public mischief, according to reports.

Mr Banerjee also said Chief Minister Suvendu Adhikari had never been seen to "appear at a police station or before a CBI court" over the Narada bribery case. He called the BJP "Bangla Birodhi", or anti-Bengal.

BJP leader Sukanta Majumdar dismissed the complaint of harassment. "This is nothing; with time he will get used to this," he said, according to reports. He said that over the last 15 years Mr Banerjee had put a lot of pressure on people and the administration.

## Background

Since the BJP formed the government in West Bengal in May, Mr Banerjee has faced several police and civic actions. On Thursday, Kolkata Municipal Corporation workers removed a police kiosk, sliding gates, CCTV cameras and flower pots outside his home, which the civic body said were illegal; he did not oppose the removal of what he called public property, but took his complaint about the wider campaign against him to the Election Commission. The Calcutta High Court has reserved its order on his challenge to the downgrading of his security cover from Z-plus.

## What happens next

Girish Park police have summoned Mr Banerjee for 20 November in a separate case over remarks in an interview that allegedly threatened police officers. The High Court's order on his security cover is awaited.
